title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, timeouts
author: Sofia Martinez
description: Motivation: Under high-concurrency workloads the continuous-batcher scheduler exhibited tail latency spikes caused by unfair queueing and long-lived requests starving short requests. This PR tunes the scheduler to improve fairness across priority classes, introduces starvation prevention heuristics, and tightens timeouts for stalled batches. Changes are conservative and gated behind configuration flags to allow a staged rollout.
commits: Refactor: scheduler loop -> split queueing, selection, and dispatch stages (atomic counters added)
Feat: add per-priority FIFO/weighted queues with aging factor and starvation detector
Tweak: configurable 'max_wait_ms' and 'preferred_batch_timeout_ms' with sensible defaults
Perf: micro-optimizations in batch selection path to reduce allocation churn
Tests: new unit + integration tests for starvation scenarios and timeouts
Docs: document new scheduler knobs and recommended production settings
Bench: add throughput/latency bench configs and CI smoke for regressions
review_comments: Ava Chen (review): Can you add metrics for per-priority queue length, avg wait, and number of starvation recoveries? Also please show perf numbers for a mixed workload (short chat vs long completion).
Author (Sofia): Added metrics (queue_length, avg_wait_ms, starvation_recoveries) and a benchmark config that simulates 80/20 short/long requests. Results included in PR description.
Liam Patel (review): The new max_wait_ms default seems aggressive for some legacy customers. Suggest exposing it in config and keeping the old behavior behind a feature flag.
Author (Sofia): Kept previous default by introducing 'scheduler.experimental_enable_aging' flag=false by default; added config and docs.
perf_results: Bench (80% short 20% long, 64 concurrent clients, r5g.8xlarge GPUs): baseline p95=320ms, p99=620ms. After changes p95=260ms (-18%), p99=540ms (-13%), throughput +6% with 1.5% CPU increase on scheduling thread. Starvation_recoveries metric shows ~0.6 recoveries/min under stress (configurable threshold).
merge_commit_message: squash: continuous-batcher scheduler tuning: improved fairness and starvation prevention - tuned timeouts, added per-priority queueing and metrics
release_notes: Continuous batcher scheduler improvements: per-priority queueing with aging, starvation prevention logic, configurable timeouts, and additional observability (queue_length, avg_wait_ms, starvation_recoveries). Reduces tail latency for mixed short/long workloads. Rollout behind experimental flag by default.
